claim: The Spindle Assembly Checkpoint (SAC) maintains genome stability during mitosis while ensuring timely anaphase onset.
source: During mitosis, the Spindle Assembly Checkpoint (SAC) maintains genome stability while also ensuring timely anaphase onset.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a general principle of SAC function.

claim: The balance between SAC strength and responsiveness is determined by the number of MELT motifs in Spc105/KNL1 and their Bub3-Bub1 binding affinities.
source: Here we show that the balance between SAC strength and responsiveness is determined by the number of 'MELT' motifs in the kinetochore protein Spc105/KNL1 and their Bub3-Bub1 binding affinities.
evidence: This is the main finding of the study as stated in the abstract.

claim: Many strong MELT motifs per Spc105/KNL1 minimize chromosome missegregation.
source: Many strong MELT motifs per Spc105/KNL1 minimize chromosome missegregation, but too many delay anaphase onset.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding of the study.

claim: Too many strong MELT motifs delay anaphase onset.
source: Many strong MELT motifs per Spc105/KNL1 minimize chromosome missegregation, but too many delay anaphase onset.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding of the study.

claim: A Spc105 variant can be constructed that trades SAC responsiveness for more accurate chromosome segregation.
source: We demonstrate this by constructing a Spc105 variant that trades SAC responsiveness for much more accurate chromosome segregation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a demonstration of the main finding.

claim: The necessity of balancing SAC strength and responsiveness drives the dual evolutionary trend of amplification of MELT motif number and degeneration of their functionally optimal amino acid sequence.
source: We propose that the necessity of balancing SAC strength and responsiveness drives the dual evolutionary trend of the amplification of MELT motif number, but degeneration of their functionally optimal amino acid sequence.
evidence: This is proposed as an explanation for evolutionary patterns observed in MELT motifs.

claim: The SAC is activated by a signaling cascade that operates from the kinetochore.
source: The SAC is activated by a signaling cascade that operates from the kinetochore, a protein structure that mediates chromosome attachment to the spindle.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: When unattached, the kinetochore produces an anaphase-inhibitory signal to delay cell division.
source: When unattached, the kinetochore produces an anaphase-inhibitory signal to delay cell division (Musacchio, 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to support it.

claim: Spc105 provides the physical scaffold for SAC signaling.
source: A key determinant of the strength of the SAC is the conserved kinetochore protein Spc105, which provides the physical scaffold for SAC signaling.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge about Spc105 function.

claim: Spc105 and its homologs possess a large, unstructured phosphodomain containing MELT motifs.
source: Spc105 and its homologs possess a large, unstructured phosphodomain containing short sequence repeats commonly referred to as 'MELT' motifs because of their consensus sequence in yeast and humans.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge about Spc105 structure.

claim: Phosphorylation of a MELT motif by Mps1 kinase turns on the SAC signaling cascade and results in generation of the anaphase-inhibitory signal.
source: Phosphorylation of a MELT motif by the conserved Mps1 kinase turns on the SAC signaling cascade and results in the generation of the anaphase-inhibitory signal (London et al., 2012; Meadows et al., 2011; Vleugel et al., 2013; Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations and reference to Figure 1A.

claim: Even just one phosphorylated MELT motif can delay anaphase in yeast and human cells.
source: Even just one phosphorylated MELT motif can delay anaphase in yeast and human cells (Aravamudhan et al., 2016; Chen et al., 2019; Krenn et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support it.

claim: The number of MELT motifs per Spc105 molecule is a crucial determinant of the strength of SAC signaling.
source: Therefore, the number of MELT motifs per Spc105 molecule is a crucial determinant of the strength of SAC signaling; many MELT motifs per Spc105 are expected to endow it, and by extension the kinetochore, with a correspondingly larger signaling capacity.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a logical inference from the previous statement about single MELT motifs.

claim: Budding yeast Spc105 contains six MELT motifs.
source: Indeed, Spc105 and its homologs typically contain many MELT motifs, for example six in budding yeast and nineteen in humans (Tromer et al., 2015)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: Human Spc105 homologs contain nineteen MELT motifs.
source: Indeed, Spc105 and its homologs typically contain many MELT motifs, for example six in budding yeast and nineteen in humans (Tromer et al., 2015)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: The large MELT motif number is thought to be essential for implementing a strong SAC.
source: Indeed, Spc105 and its homologs typically contain many MELT motifs, for example six in budding yeast and nineteen in humans (Tromer et al., 2015), and the large MELT motif number is thought to be essential for implementing a strong SAC (Chen et al., 2019; Krenn et al., 2014; Vleugel et al., 2015; Vleugel et al., 2013; Zhang et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with multiple citations.

claim: Only ~20% of MELT motifs in budding yeast engage in SAC signaling when cells are treated with high doses of nocodazole.
source: However, when budding yeast and human cells are treated with high doses of the microtubule poison nocodazole, only a small fraction of the MELT motifs,~20 and~35% respectively, engage in SAC signaling, and even fewer MELT motifs are sufficient for arresting cell division (Aravamudhan et al., 2016; Vleugel et al., 2015; Vleugel et al., 2013; Zhang et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: Only ~35% of MELT motifs in human cells engage in SAC signaling when cells are treated with high doses of nocodazole.
source: However, when budding yeast and human cells are treated with high doses of the microtubule poison nocodazole, only a small fraction of the MELT motifs,~20 and~35% respectively, engage in SAC signaling, and even fewer MELT motifs are sufficient for arresting cell division (Aravamudhan et al., 2016; Vleugel et al., 2015; Vleugel et al., 2013; Zhang et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: Three of the six motifs in budding yeast Spc105 possess the consensus amino acid sequence 'MELT'.
source: Three of the six motifs in the budding yeast Spc105 possess the consensus amino acid sequence ('MELT'), and these are likely to display higher Bub3-Bub1 binding affinity than the other three motifs possessing divergent amino acid sequences (London et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation.

claim: MELT motifs with consensus sequence are likely to display higher Bub3-Bub1 binding affinity than motifs with divergent sequences.
source: Three of the six motifs in the budding yeast Spc105 possess the consensus amino acid sequence ('MELT'), and these are likely to display higher Bub3-Bub1 binding affinity than the other three motifs possessing divergent amino acid sequences (London et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation.

claim: Motif #2 and #6 support robust SAC signaling as judged by the ability of mutant cells to maintain 2N ploidy over 4 hr of nocodazole-induced mitotic arrest.
source: Motif #2 and #6 supported robust SAC signaling as judged by the ability of the mutant cells to maintain 2N ploidy over the 4 hr long duration of the nocodazole-induced mitotic arrest despite recruiting ~50% less Bub1 compared to wild-type Spc105 (the leftmost graph in Figure 1D, the small fraction of 4N ploidy cells emerging after >2 hr of nocodazole treatment represents cells that slipped out of the SAC arrest).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 1D showing flow cytometry data.

claim: Motif #2 and #6 recruit ~50% less Bub1 compared to wild-type Spc105.
source: Motif #2 and #6 supported robust SAC signaling as judged by the ability of the mutant cells to maintain 2N ploidy over the 4 hr long duration of the nocodazole-induced mitotic arrest despite recruiting ~50% less Bub1 compared to wild-type Spc105 (the leftmost graph in Figure 1D, the small fraction of 4N ploidy cells emerging after >2 hr of nocodazole treatment represents cells that slipped out of the SAC arrest).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 1C showing Bub1 recruitment data.

claim: Motif #4 recruited significantly less Bub1-mCherry than motifs #2 and #6.
source: Motif #4 recruited significantly less Bub1-mCherry than the other two, which is consistent with its weaker affinity for binding recombinant Bub3-Bub1 complex in vitro (Overlack et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 1C and a citation.

claim: Motif #4 resulted in a weaker SAC as evidenced by the emergence of a considerable fraction of tetraploid cells 3-4 hr post nocodazole treatment.
source: It also resulted in a weaker SAC as evidenced by the emergence of a considerable fraction of tetraploid cells 3–4 hr post treatment.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 1D.

claim: Replacement of the divergent amino acid sequence of motif #4 ('IDLT') with the consensus sequence ('MELT') improved both Bub1 recruitment and SAC strength.
source: Replacement of the divergent amino acid sequence of this motif ('IDLT') with the consensus sequence ('MELT') improved both Bub1 recruitment and SAC strength.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 1C-D.

claim: The amino acid sequence of each MELT motif primarily determines its ability to recruit Bub3-Bub1 and its contribution to SAC signaling.
source: Thus, the amino acid sequence of each MELT motif primarily determines its ability to recruit Bub3-Bub1 and its contribution to SAC signaling (Figure 1C–D).
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the data in Figure 1C-D.

claim: Just one strong MELT motif per Spc105 is sufficient to induce a prolonged mitotic arrest upon spindle depolymerization by nocodazole.
source: Furthermore, just one strong MELT motif per Spc105 is sufficient to induce a prolonged mitotic arrest upon spindle depolymerization by nocodazole.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the nocodazole experiments.

claim: Low doses of benomyl increase microtubule dynamicity and challenge spindle formation and chromosome biorientation.
source: Unlike nocodazole treatment, which destroys the spindle, benomyl at low concentrations increases microtubule dynamicity and therefore challenges spindle formation and chromosome biorientation.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the benomyl experiments.

claim: Wild-type cells can still grow in low concentrations of benomyl, but genetic defects in SAC signaling or chromosome biorientation can cause poor growth or inviability.
source: Wild-type cells still grow under this condition, but any genetic defects in SAC signaling or chromosome biorientation can cause poor growth or inviability (Hoyt et al., 1991).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation.

claim: In normal media, yeast cells released from G1 arrest bioriented chromosome IV in ~45 min and completed anaphase by 75 min.
source: In normal media, yeast cells released from a G1 arrest bioriented chromosome IV in ~45 min and completed anaphase by 75 min.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 2A.

claim: In media containing low doses of benomyl, chromosome IV biorientation and anaphase were significantly delayed.
source: In media containing low doses of benomyl, both events were significantly delayed.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 2A.

claim: In most cells treated with benomyl, chromosome IV did not achieve biorientation even after 105 min post release.
source: In most cells, chromosome IV did not achieve biorientation even after 105 min post release (the duration of the experiment was limited to 105 min, because cells not affected by the treatment entered the next cell cycle after this point, which complicated the analysis).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 2A.

claim: Most cells treated with benomyl contained a significantly smaller number of unattached kinetochores recruiting Bub1-mCherry compared to nocodazole-treated cells.
source: Most cells contained a significantly smaller number of unattached kinetochores recruiting Bub1-mCherry. Importantly, the number of unattached kinetochores per cell was significantly smaller when compared to the average number of unattached kinetochores per cell after nocodazole treatment (5 +/- 4 per cell versus to ~10 in nocodazole-treated cells (Aravamudhan et al., 2016; Figure 2A right).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 2A and a citation.

claim: 75 min after release from G1 arrest into benomyl-containing media, more mutant cells expressing Spc105 with motif #2 and #6 were in anaphase compared to wild-type cells.
source: However, 75 min after release from the G1 arrest into media containing benomyl more mutant cells were in anaphase compared to wild-type cells, as evidenced by elongated spindles and sister kinetochores segregated in the mother and bud (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 2B.

claim: Many cells expressing Spc105 with motif #2 and #6 are unable to prevent anaphase onset even though they contain small numbers of unattached kinetochores.
source: Therefore, these observations together imply that many cells expressing Spc105 with motif #2 and #6 are unable to prevent anaphase onset even though they contain small numbers of unattached kinetochores.
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the data in Figure 2B.

claim: Strains expressing Spc105 mutants with either motif #2 alone or motif #2 and #6 together grew at slower rates and reached significantly lower cell densities than wild-type strain in benomyl-containing media.
source: Strains expressing Spc105 mutants with either motif #2 alone or motif #2 and #6 together grew at slower rates and reached significantly lower cell densities than the wild-type strain.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 2C.

claim: Spc105 mutants containing either the first two or three MELT motifs supported nearly normal growth in benomyl-containing media.
source: Spc105 mutants containing either the first two or three MELT motifs (two of which possess the consensus amino acid sequence, and hence are expected to be strong), supported nearly normal growth in benomyl-containing media.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 2C.

claim: The Spc105 mutant with only the last three MELT motifs active grew more slowly and reached lower maximal cell density in benomyl-containing media.
source: Interestingly, the Spc105 mutant with only the last three MELT motifs active grew more slowly and reached lower maximal cell density.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 2C.

claim: At least two strong MELT motifs are necessary for cell survival in cells containing a small number of unattached kinetochores.
source: They suggest that in cells containing a small number of unattached kinetochores at least two, strong MELT motifs are necessary for cell survival, and the presence of all six MELT motifs in Spc105 ensures maximal population growth.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the benomyl growth experiments.

claim: The presence of all six MELT motifs in Spc105 ensures maximal population growth.
source: They suggest that in cells containing a small number of unattached kinetochores at least two, strong MELT motifs are necessary for cell survival, and the presence of all six MELT motifs in Spc105 ensures maximal population growth.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the benomyl growth experiments.

claim: The amino acid sequence, and not the position of MELT motifs in the phosphodomain, is the sole determinant of their SAC signaling activity.
source: Thus, the amino acid sequence, and not the position of MELT motifs in the phosphodomain, is the sole determinant of their SAC signaling activity.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the position-swap experiments in Figure 2E.

claim: Chromosome missegregation events were significantly more frequent in cells expressing Spc105#4-6 compared to wild-type strain.
source: We found that chromosome missegregation events were significantly more frequent in cells expressing Spc105#4-6 compared a wild-type strain (we scored both half-sectored and fully red colonies as chromosome mis-segregation events; see Materials and methods for details).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 2F.

claim: Chromosome missegregation events in cells expressing Spc105#4-6 were more frequent even when compared to the mad1∆ strain lacking a functional SAC.
source: In fact, they were more frequent even when compared to the mad1∆ strain lacking a functional SAC (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 2F.

claim: The higher missegregation frequency in Spc105#4-6 mutant is likely due to lower Sgo1 recruitment which impairs chromosome biorientation.
source: The most likely explanation for the higher missegregation frequency in this mutant is that the kinetochores in prometaphase recruit lower amounts of Bub3-Bub1, and therefore, lower amounts of Sgo1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 3C–D). The lower Sgo1 recruitment ultimately impairs chromosome biorientation, and thus further elevates chromosome missegregation frequency.
evidence: This is stated as an explanation with reference to supplementary figures.

claim: Spc105 containing more than one strong MELT motif is essential to ensure accurate chromosome segregation during normal cell division.
source: These results demonstrate that Spc105 containing more than one, strong MELT motif is essential to ensure accurate chromosome segregation during normal cell division.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the chromosome loss assay results.

claim: In cells containing a large and unchanging number of unattached kinetochores, defects in the signaling output of individual kinetochores can be masked by the cumulative signaling output of many simultaneously signaling kinetochores.
source: They also suggest that in cells containing a large and unchanging number of unattached kinetochores, defects in the signaling output of individual kinetochores (e.g. due to Spc105 containing weak MELT motifs) can be masked by the cumulative signaling output of many, simultaneously signaling kinetochores.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the comparison of nocodazole and benomyl experiments.

claim: The structure of the MELpT-Bub3-Bub1 complex shows that the phosphorylated threonine residue is lodged in a positively charged groove on Bub3 surface.
source: The structure of the MELpT-Bub3-Bub1289-359 complex shows that the phosphorylated threonine residue is lodged in a positively charged groove on Bub3 surface (Primorac et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 1B and a citation.

claim: The Bub3-Bub1 complex will sterically interfere with PP1 by shielding the phosphothreonine in the MELT motif.
source: This mode of binding implies that the Bub3-Bub1 complex will sterically interfere with PP1 by shielding the phosphothreonine in the MELT motif (see Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the structural data.

claim: The rate of dephosphorylation of a MELT motif may be inversely correlated with its Bub3-Bub1 binding affinity.
source: Consequently, the rate of dephosphorylation of a MELT motif may be inversely correlated with its Bub3-Bub1 binding affinity, and by extension, its amino acid sequence.
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis based on the structural inference.

claim: Sequence divergence of some MELT motifs may be desirable because it allows mutants to trade SAC strength for responsiveness, achieving timely anaphase onset and rapid growth.
source: Given that only two strong MELT motifs are sufficient for a strong SAC, sequence divergence of some of the MELT motifs may be desirable, because this allows the mutants to trade SAC strength for responsiveness, achieving timely anaphase onset and hence a rapid growth.
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis to explain the evolutionary pattern.

claim: In budding yeast, Mps1 kinase binds to the CH-domains of Ndc80 even after end-on attachments form.
source: In budding yeast, Mps1 kinase binds to the CH-domains of Ndc80 even after end-on attachments form (Aravamudhan et al., 2015; Koch et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated with citations.

claim: A gradient of Mps1 kinase activity is likely to exist in bioriented yeast kinetochores.
source: This implies that a gradient of Mps1 kinase activity is likely to exist in bioriented yeast kinetochores.
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the persistence of Mps1 binding.

claim: Weak FRET was detected between Spc105222:GFP and Dad4-mCherry.
source: We detected weak FRET between Spc105222:GFP (GFP inserted after amino acid 222 in Spc105) and Dad4-mCherry (a subunit of the Dam1 complex, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated with reference to supplementary figure showing FRET data.

claim: Spc105 phosphodomain can extend past its average position toward the high Mps1 kinase activity region of the kinetochore.
source: This result suggest that Spc105 phosphodomain can extend past its average position toward the high Mps1 kinase activity region of the kinetochore (Aravamudhan et al., 2014; Joglekar et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the FRET data with citations.

claim: The phosphodomain tethered distally from the CH-domains was robustly phosphorylated as evidenced by the recruitment of Bub3-mCherry.
source: Consistent with our hypothesis, even though the phosphodomain did not activate the SAC when tethered distally from the CH-domains (e.g. at the C terminus of Ndc80), it was robustly phosphorylated as evidenced by the recruitment of Bub3-mCherry (Figure 3A and B, also see Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 3A and B.

claim: Bub3-mCherry recruitment decreased progressively as the average separation between the tethering point and the CH-domains increased.
source: Bub3-mCherry recruitment decreased progressively as the average separation between the tethering point and the CH-domains increased (as measured in bioriented kinetochores, Joglekar et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 3B and a citation.

claim: The inclusion of the PP1 recruitment motif in Spc105 reduced, but did not eliminate, Bub3 recruitment.
source: The inclusion of the PP1 recruitment motif in Spc105 (+PP1) reduced, but did not eliminate, Bub3 recruitment (+PP1 in Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 3A and supplementary figure.

claim: A sizeable fraction (~20%) of anaphase cells displayed Bub3-mCherry colocalized with kinetochores when the phosphodomain was tethered with PP1 recruitment motif.
source: In fact, a sizeable fraction (~20%) of anaphase cells displayed Bub3-mCherry colocalized with kinetochores.
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 3A.

claim: The phosphodomain recruited Bub3-mCherry even when tethered after kinetochore biorientation in metaphase arrested cells.
source: Finally, the phosphodomain recruited Bub3-mCherry even when we tethered it after kinetochore biorientation in metaphase arrested cells indicating that not all of the Bub3 was recruited prior to biorientation (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 3C.

claim: The phosphodomain did not recruit Mad1 when tethered to a position distal to the CH-domains.
source: Importantly, we found that the phosphodomain did not recruit Mad1 when it was tethered to a position distal to the CH-domains (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 3D.

claim: A diminishing gradient of Mps1 kinase activity extends from the CH-domains toward the centromere in bioriented yeast kinetochores.
source: These experiments show that a diminishing gradient of Mps1 kinase activity extends from the CH-domains toward the centromere in bioriented yeast kinetochores, and this residual Mps1 kinase activity likely continues to phosphorylate the MELT motifs.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the tethering experiments.

claim: The residual Mps1 activity likely continues to phosphorylate the MELT motifs in bioriented kinetochores.
source: These experiments show that a diminishing gradient of Mps1 kinase activity extends from the CH-domains toward the centromere in bioriented yeast kinetochores, and this residual Mps1 kinase activity likely continues to phosphorylate the MELT motifs.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the tethering experiments.

claim: The absence of Mad1 recruitment in tethering experiments suggests that the residual Mps1 activity is not sufficient to phosphorylate Bub1.
source: The absence of Mad1 recruitment in these experiments suggests that the residual Mps1 activity is not sufficient to phosphorylate Bub1.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the lack of Mad1 recruitment.

claim: The reduction of Mps1 activity after microtubule attachment primes the SAC for silencing.
source: In conclusion, the reduction of Mps1 activity after microtubule attachment primes the SAC for silencing.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the experiments.

claim: The reduction of Mps1 activity is not sufficient to induce anaphase onset; PP1 ensures timely anaphase onset.
source: However, but this is not sufficient to induce anaphase onset; PP1 ensures timely anaphase onset.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the experiments.

claim: Bioriented kinetochores in spc105RASA strain recruited both Bub3 and Mad1.
source: This was confirmed by the examination the recruitment of SAC proteins in strains expressing spc105RASA, wherein Spc105 cannot recruit PP1 (Rosenberg et al., 2011). Bioriented kinetochores in this strain recruited both Bub3 and Mad1 (Figure 4B, note that the spc105RASA mutation results in lethality unless the SAC is inactivated).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 4B and a citation.

claim: The spc105RASA bub1453A, 455A double mutant was viable.
source: The spc105RASA bub1453A, 455A double mutant was viable, indicating that the dephosphorylation of Bub1 by PP1 aids SAC silencing (Figure 4C, plate photographs).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 4C showing tetrad dissection.

claim: The dephosphorylation of Bub1 by PP1 aids SAC silencing.
source: The spc105RASA bub1453A, 455A double mutant was viable, indicating that the dephosphorylation of Bub1 by PP1 aids SAC silencing (Figure 4C, plate photographs).
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the viability of the double mutant.

claim: The SAC was still active in the spc105RASA bub1453A, 455A double mutant as judged by the ability to maintain 2N ploidy upon prolonged nocodazole treatment.
source: Surprisingly, however, the SAC was still active in this double mutant as judged by the ability of this strain to maintain 2N ploidy upon a prolonged nocodazole treatment (Figure 4C, 2nd plot from the left) and to grow in benomyl-containing media (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 4C and supplementary figure.

claim: Mad1 recruitment to unattached kinetochores in nocodazole-treated cells was diminished, but not eliminated in the spc105RASA bub1453A, 455A double mutant.
source: Consistently, Mad1 recruitment to unattached kinetochores in nocodazole-treated cells was diminished, but not eliminated (Figure 4C, scatter plot, second from the right).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 4C.

claim: The spc105RASA bub1453A, 455A double mutant exhibited a longer doubling time in YPD, which is suggestive of a SAC silencing defect.
source: The spc105RASA bub1453A, 455A double mutant exhibited a longer doubling time in YPD, which is suggestive of a SAC silencing defect arising from the lack of PP1 recruitment by Spc105 (Figure 4C, scatter plot on the right).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 4C.

claim: PP1-mediated dephosphorylation of several phosphorylated residues on Bub1 suppresses Mad1 recruitment and thereby contributes to the responsiveness of the SAC to silencing.
source: Thus, PP1-mediated dephosphorylation of several phosphorylated residues on Bub1 suppresses Mad1 recruitment and thereby contributes to the responsiveness of the SAC to silencing.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the Bub1 phosphosite mutant experiments.

claim: The efficiency of SAC silencing likely depends on the effectiveness of PP1-mediated dephosphorylation of the MELT motifs versus Bub1.
source: Therefore, the efficiency of SAC silencing likely depends on the effectiveness of PP1-mediated dephosphorylation of the MELT motifs versus Bub1.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the comparison of MELT and Bub1 dephosphorylation.

claim: PP1 must dephosphorylate multiple sites in Bub1 to completely inhibit Mad1 recruitment.
source: PP1 must dephosphorylate multiple sites in Bub1 to completely inhibit Mad1 recruitment, whereas the dephosphorylation of just one residue in the MELT motif prevents the recruitment of both Bub3-Bub1 and Mad1.
evidence: This is stated as a comparison of the requirements for silencing via Bub1 vs MELT motifs.

claim: The dephosphorylation of just one residue in the MELT motif prevents the recruitment of both Bub3-Bub1 and Mad1.
source: PP1 must dephosphorylate multiple sites in Bub1 to completely inhibit Mad1 recruitment, whereas the dephosphorylation of just one residue in the MELT motif prevents the recruitment of both Bub3-Bub1 and Mad1.
evidence: This is stated as a comparison of the requirements for silencing via Bub1 vs MELT motifs.

claim: The responsiveness of SAC silencing will be determined by the PP1-mediated dephosphorylation of MELT motifs rather than Bub1.
source: This implies that the responsiveness of SAC silencing will be determined by the PP1-mediated dephosphorylation of MELT motifs rather than Bub1.
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the comparison of MELT and Bub1 dephosphorylation requirements.

claim: If Bub3-Bub1-binding to the MELT motif interferes with MELT motif dephosphorylation, then the affinity of each MELT motif for Bub3-Bub1 will strongly influence the efficiency of its dephosphorylation.
source: Therefore, if Bub3-Bub1-binding to the MELT motif itself interferes with MELT motif dephosphorylation, then the affinity of each MELT motif for Bub3-Bub1, and hence its sequence, will strongly influence the efficiency of its dephosphorylation.
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis about the mechanism of MELT motif dephosphorylation.

claim: In a large fraction of cells expressing #16, Bub1-mCherry abnormally colocalized with bioriented kinetochore clusters indicating a defect in SAC silencing.
source: In a large fraction of cells expressing #16, Bub1-mCherry abnormally colocalized with bioriented kinetochore clusters indicating a defect in SAC silencing (Figure 5A, left and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 5A and supplementary figure.

claim: The doubling time for #16 strains was ~14% higher compared to wild-type cells (164 vs 144 min).
source: Accordingly, the doubling time for these strains was ~14% higher compared to wild-type cells (164 vs 144 min.; Figure 5A, middle scatter plot).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 5A.

claim: The increased doubling time in #16 strains is due to the SAC, because deletion of MAD1 eliminated it.
source: The increased doubling time is due to the SAC, because the deletion of MAD1 eliminated it (5A, second from the right).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 5A.

claim: The stronger SAC activity of #16 did not confer any detectable advantage in benomyl-containing media.
source: However, the stronger SAC activity of #16 did not confer any detectable advantage to yeast cells: in media containing benomyl the growth rate and maximal cell density reached was similar for both wild-type and #16 strains (Figure 5A right).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 5A.

claim: The retardation of the cell cycle due to the hyper-active Spc105 allele is a fitness cost for the yeast strain.
source: Therefore, the retardation of the cell cycle due to the hyper-active Spc105 allele is a fitness cost for this yeast strain, and too many high affinity MELT motifs per Spc105 are likely to be counterproductive.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the #16 experiments.

claim: Too many high affinity MELT motifs per Spc105 are likely to be counterproductive.
source: Therefore, the retardation of the cell cycle due to the hyper-active Spc105 allele is a fitness cost for this yeast strain, and too many high affinity MELT motifs per Spc105 are likely to be counterproductive.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the #16 experiments.

claim: Upon partial induction of Bub1 overexpression, kinetochores retained Bub1 even after biorientation in both wild-type and #16 strains.
source: Upon partial induction of the GAL1 promoter using a low galactose concentration (0.5%, that is moderate Bub1 over-expression), kinetochores retained Bub1 even after biorientation in both strains (micrographs in Figure 5B, left).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 5B.

claim: The doubling time of cell cultures of both wild-type and #16 strains was significantly higher upon Bub1 overexpression, but the effect was more severe for the #16 culture.
source: The doubling time of cell cultures of both strains was significantly higher, but the effect was more severe for the #16 culture (Figure 5B, ; Figure 5—figure supplement 1A left).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 5B and supplementary figure.

claim: The fold-increase in doubling time was higher for #16 cultures compared to wild-type cell cultures in both partial and full induction conditions.
source: Importantly, the fold-increase in the doubling time was higher for the #16 cultures compared to wild-type cell cultures in both experiments (~15% for wild-type Spc105 with either partial or full induction of the GAL1 promoter, 35% and 66% for #16 in partial and full induction conditions respectively).
evidence: This is stated as a quantitative comparison of the effects of Bub1 overexpression.

claim: The low expression level of Bub1 limits the recruitment of Bub3-Bub1 and Mad1-Mad2 to unattached yeast kinetochores and thus primarily limits SAC strength.
source: These experiment along with our prior observations showing that Bub1 abundance primarily limits Mad1 recruitment to the cell show that the low expression level of Bub1 limits the recruitment of Bub3-Bub1 and Mad1-Mad2 to unattached yeast kinetochores and thus primarily limits SAC strength.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the Bub1 overexpression experiments.

claim: The number and affinity of MELT motifs determines both the strength and the responsiveness of the SAC to PP1-mediated silencing.
source: The number and affinity of MELT motifs determines both the strength and the responsiveness of the SAC to PP1-mediated silencing.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the experiments.

claim: Only the weaker MELT motifs (#4-6) suppressed the lethality caused by the non-functional RVSF motif.
source: Tetrad dissection analysis of the two diploid strains: SPC105/spc105Δ leu2/leu2::spc105RASA,#1-3 and SPC105/spc105Δ leu2/leu2::spc105RASA,#4-6 revealed that only the weaker MELT motifs suppressed the lethality caused by the non-functional RVSF motif (Figure 6A, also see Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 6A and supplementary figure.

claim: Diffusive interactions between PP1 and Spc105 appear to be sufficient to dephosphorylate the weak MELT motifs, but not for the strong motifs.
source: Thus, diffusive interactions between PP1 and Spc105 appear to be sufficient to dephosphorylate the weak MELT motifs, but not for the strong motifs.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the tetrad dissection results.

claim: The simplest explanation for the rescue of spc105RASA by weak MELT motifs is that Bub3-Bub1 binding to the MELT motif hampers the ability of PP1 to dephosphorylate the MELT motif.
source: The simplest explanation this observation is that Bub3-Bub1 binding to the MELT motif hampers the ability of PP1 to dephosphorylate the MELT motif.
evidence: This is stated as an explanation for the differential rescue by weak vs strong MELT motifs.

claim: Kinetochores in the spc105#4-6RASA strain did not recruit Bub3-mCherry in metaphase, but recruited both Bub3 and Mad1 when unattached upon nocodazole treatment.
source: Using fluorescence microscopy, we confirmed that kinetochores in the spc105#4-6 strain did not recruit Bub3-mCherry in metaphase, but recruited both Bub3 and Mad1 when unattached upon nocodazole treatment (Figure 6B, also see Figure 5—figure supplement 1D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 6B and supplementary figures.

claim: The SAC in spc105#4-6RASA strain was sufficient to maintain 2N ploidy during prolonged nocodazole treatment.
source: As expected, the SAC was sufficient to maintain 2N ploidy during prolonged nocodazole treatment (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 6B.

claim: The spc105#4-6RASA strain grew significantly faster than wild-type strain in benomyl-containing media, suggesting improved chromosome biorientation and segregation accuracy.
source: In benomyl-containing media, this strain grew significantly faster even compared to the wild-type strain, suggesting that chromosome biorientation and chromosome segregation accuracy in this strain was improved (6C).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 6C.

claim: The chromosome segregation accuracy in spc105#4-6RASA strain was significantly higher than the strain expressing spc105#4-6 and even wild-type cells.
source: Colony sectoring assay revealed that even under normal growth conditions, the chromosome segregation accuracy in this strain was significantly higher than the strain expressing spc105#4-6 and even wild-type cells (only three red colonies out of ~6600 compared to 18 red colonies out of ~5100 for the wild-type strain, Figure 6E).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 6E.

claim: The doubling time for spc105#4-6RASA mutant under normal conditions was 20% higher than wild-type cells.
source: However, the doubling time for this mutant under normal conditions was 20% higher than wild-type cells, (Figure 6D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1F ).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 6D and supplementary figure.

claim: The higher doubling time in spc105#4-6RASA is likely due to an SAC silencing defect.
source: The higher doubling time is likely due to an SAC silencing defect, although this needs to be confirmed experimentally.
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis that needs experimental confirmation.

claim: The balance of SAC signaling strength and its responsiveness to silencing mechanisms determines the trade-off between accurate chromosome segregation and timely anaphase onset.
source: These observations demonstrate that the balance of SAC signaling strength and its responsiveness to silencing mechanisms determines the trade-off between accurate chromosome segregation and timely anaphase onset.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the engineered Spc105 variant experiments.

claim: The phosphodomain tethered at Ndc80-C robustly recruited Mad1 in cells expressing spc105RASA, #4-6 but not wild-type Spc105.
source: Consistent with this expectation, we found that the phosphodomain tethered at Ndc80-C robustly recruited Mad1 in cells expressing spc105RASA, #4-6 but not wild-type Spc105 (Figure 6F, representative images at the middle, bar graph at the bottom left).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 6F.

claim: The growth rate of cells expressing spc105RASA, #4-6, but not wild-type Spc105, in media containing rapamycin was reduced, revealing incomplete SAC silencing.
source: The growth rate of cells expressing the spc105RASA, #4-6, but not wild-type Spc105 in media containing rapamycin was also reduced, revealing incomplete SAC silencing (6F, bottom right).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 6F.

claim: The reduction of Mps1 kinase activity in the kinetochore primes the SAC for silencing, enabling PP1 to disrupt SAC protein recruitment.
source: These experiments demonstrate that the reduction of Mps1 kinase activity in the kinetochore primes the SAC for silencing, enabling PP1 to disrupt SAC protein recruitment.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the tethering experiments with spc105RASA, #4-6.

claim: The reduced SAC strength due to Spc105 mutants containing fewer or only weak MELT motifs is apparent only in normally growing cells or when chromosome biorientation is challenged.
source: First, we find that the reduced SAC strength due to Spc105 mutants containing fewer or only the weak MELT motifs is apparent only in normally growing cells or when the process of chromosome biorientation is challenged.
evidence: This is stated as a key insight in the Discussion.

claim: Reduced SAC strength is not detected in nocodazole-treated cells containing a large and constant number of unattached chromosomes.
source: It is not detected in nocodazole-treated cells containing a large and constant number of unattached chromosomes.
evidence: This is stated as a key insight in the Discussion.

claim: The cumulative signaling output of large and unchanging number of unattached kinetochores in nocodazole-treated cells masks the reduced signaling output of individual kinetochores.
source: The most likely explanation for this discrepancy is that the cumulative signaling output of the large and unchanging number of unattached kinetochores in nocodazole-treated cells masks the reduced signaling output of individual kinetochores.
evidence: This is stated as an explanation for the discrepancy between nocodazole and benomyl experiments.

claim: SAC strength measured as the duration of mitotic arrest in nocodazole-treated cells is not useful in predicting the ability of the SAC to ensure genome stability.
source: Therefore, SAC strength measured as the duration of mitotic arrest in nocodazole-treated cells is not useful in predicting the ability of the SAC to ensure genome stability.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the Discussion.

claim: Under normal conditions, the maintenance of genomic stability in budding yeast requires a strong SAC enabled by more than one MELT motif possessing the functionally optimal amino acid sequence.
source: Under normal conditions, the maintenance of genomic stability in budding yeast requires a strong SAC enabled by more than one MELT motif possessing the functionally optimal amino acid sequence.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the Discussion.

claim: This insight provides a functional explanation for the evolutionary trend of the expansion of the number of MELT motifs in Spc105 and its homologs via recurrent duplication events.
source: This insight provides a functional explanation for the evolutionary trend of the expansion of the number of MELT motifs in Spc105 and its homologs via recurrent duplication events (Tromer et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the findings in evolutionary context with a citation.

claim: The microtubule-mediated separation and dissociation of Mps1 significantly reduces its kinase activity, especially in the inner kinetochore beyond the Dam1 complex.
source: The microtubule-mediated separation and dissociation of Mps1 significantly reduces its kinase activity, especially in the inner kinetochore beyond the Dam1 complex (Aravamudhan et al., 2015; Hiruma et al., 2015; Ji et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citations.

claim: The residual Mps1 activity can drive SAC signaling at a lower level and retard mitotic progression.
source: The residual Mps1 activity can drive SAC signaling at a lower level and retard mitotic progression.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as an interpretation of the findings.

claim: PP1 recruited by Spc105 dephosphorylates the MELT motifs and Bub1 to stop the recruitment of Bub1 and Mad1 to the kinetochore.
source: This is prevented by the PP1 recruited by Spc105, which dephosphorylates the MELT motifs and Bub1 to stop the recruitment of Bub1 and Mad1 to the kinetochore.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a summary of the findings.

claim: Bub1 dephosphorylation contributes to SAC silencing, however, MELT motif dephosphorylation by PP1 has a stronger impact on SAC silencing.
source: Bub1 dephosphorylation contributes to SAC silencing, however, MELT motif dephosphorylation by PP1 has a stronger impact on SAC silencing, consistent with the foundational role of the MELT motifs in the SAC signaling cascade.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a summary of the findings.

claim: The number and activity of MELT motifs can be suitably balanced to make the dedicated mechanism for PP1 recruitment via Spc105 non-essential.
source: With this insight, we demonstrate that the number and activity of MELT motifs can be suitably balanced to make the dedicated mechanism for PP1 recruitment via Spc105 non-essential.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a summary of the findings.

claim: The elimination of the Spc105-PP1 interaction has a significant advantage: chromosome biorientation and error correction are improved under stressed conditions.
source: In fact, the elimination of this interaction has a significant advantage: chromosome biorientation and error correction are improved under stressed conditions.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a summary of the findings.

claim: The elimination of Spc105-PP1 interaction comes at the cost of delayed SAC silencing under normal conditions.
source: However, this comes at the cost of delayed SAC silencing under normal conditions.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a summary of the findings.

claim: When the MELT motif is bound by Bub3-Bub1, steric effects are likely to interfere with its dephosphorylation.
source: When the MELT motif is bound by Bub3-Bub1, steric effects are likely to interfere with its dephosphorylation.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a hypothesis.

claim: The high affinity MELT motifs in Spc105 are more resistant to PP1-mediated dephosphorylation and they reduce the responsiveness of the SAC to silencing.
source: Nevertheless, its main predictions are supported by our data: the high affinity MELT motifs in Spc105 are more resistant to PP1-mediated dephosphorylationand they reduce the responsiveness of the SAC to silencing.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a summary of the findings.

claim: At a minimum, the signaling output of one unattached kinetochore has to be sufficient to delay anaphase onset until stable, end-on microtubule attachment is formed.
source: It is important to note that at a minimum, the signaling output of one unattached kinetochore has to be sufficient to delay anaphase onset until stable, end-on microtubule attachment is formed.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a logical requirement for SAC function.

claim: Beyond a certain limit, additional signaling capacity does not offer any advantage; it is likely to increase the duration of the cell cycle unnecessarily.
source: Beyond this limit, additional signaling capacity does not offer any advantage; it is likely to increase the duration of the cell cycle unnecessarily.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a logical inference.

claim: Beyond a certain number, additional MELT motifs per Spc105 do not contribute to the strength of the SAC and are likely to impose a fitness cost.
source: Therefore, beyond a certain number, additional MELT motifs per Spc105 do not contribute to the strength of the SAC. Instead, they are likely to impose a fitness cost.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a conclusion.

claim: The number and Bub3-Bub1 binding affinity of MELT motifs must be optimized to balance SAC strength and responsiveness.
source: Therefore, the number and Bub3-Bub1 binding affinity of MELT motifs must be optimized to balance SAC strength and responsiveness.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a conclusion.

claim: The evolution of MELT motif copy number and sequence may reflect an evolutionary process that balances SAC strength and responsiveness to ensure genomic stability and timely cell division.
source: We propose that the evolution of MELT motif copy number and sequence may reflect an evolutionary process that balances SAC strength and responsiveness to ensure genomic stability and timely cell division.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a proposal about evolutionary mechanisms.
